analysis: The only change in this batch is documentation in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1129-1141). It describes Qwen inline MTP assistant behavior: ordinary decode rows can chain, the target forward returns hidden rows, finalize appends them to the assistant history, and the carry is stored. It adds two rollback env switches, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY, and a per-drafter opt-in, supportsOrdinaryDecodeHistory. No code, configuration defaults, endpoints or trust-boundary logic change in this batch. I found no regression in the documentation text itself. Relevant threats are TB-007 and T-041 (prefix cache and checkpoint behavior), T-028 (residual GPU memory) and T-010 (cancellation). The doc says rows keep the committed-observation fence and native completion tracking for drafters that need them. It does not say the prefix-cache identity or SSD checkpoint contract changed. The behavior it describes is in-memory assistant history and carry state, so it does not clearly widen the at-rest surface. The underlying Swift change (EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift) is not in this batch. Integration should check that the assistant history and carry created on chained decode are request-scoped. They must be cleared on cancellation, completion and request-membership change, so they are not shared across tenants. They must also stay out of SSD checkpoint capture, or be covered by the existing CBv2MTPPrefixCheckpointCoding validation. The unmodified documentation of the SSD cache path and its T-041 mitigations is consistent with this change. Because the code was not supplied, the code-side contract remains unverified.
